newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Submarine optic cables to link Nigeria oil region.
newsitem.headline: Submarine optic cables to link Nigeria oil region.

text.p: Nigeria on Monday began laying a fibre optic cable to upgrade dire telecommunications in its southeastern oil-producing areas and form part of a projected loop around Africa.
Minister of Communications Major-General Tajudeen Olanrewaju said the project would cost DM 194 million ($125 million) and be handled by German firm Siemens.
He said the project will eventually become part of Africa One Project, planned to link Africa's coastal cities with a fibre optic ring.
Commercial capital Lagos will be linked with Port-Harcourt, passing via the oil-rich Niger Delta, with a total of over 800 kilometres of optic fibre cable.
"This project is a welcome development to the oil-producing companies which depend very much on data for their activities in the oil-producing areas," said Olanrewaju.
Wolfgang Giebel, head of Siemens operations team, said it would take 14 months for work to be completed on the telecommunications project.
The cable system will be laid along the coast in six links -- four in the Bight of Benin Channels and two in the river sections, Giebel said.

"The submarine cables will be buried into the seabed by special machines to protect them from any damages. They offer a total of 26 fibres each and are able to transmit 7,860 telephone channels simultaneously as well as television signals."

Telecommunications in Africa's most populous country of 100 million are notoriously unreliable. But the sector, until now operated by state monopoly Nigeria Telecommunications (NITEL), is gradually opening up to private enterprise.
NITEL in July signed inter-connection agreements with five firms and gave them provisional licences, though they are yet to commence operations.
